text: A can complete a work in 12 days, B in 18 days. They start together, but after 4 days, A leaves. C joins B and finishes the remaining work in 6 days. In how many days can C alone complete the whole work?
A can complete a work in 10 days. B is 50% more efficient than A. If they work together, in how many days will the work be completed?
explanation: A's rate = 1/10. B is 50% more efficient, so B's rate = 1.5 × 1/10 = 3/20. Together: 1/10 + 3/20 = 2/20 + 3/20 = 5/20 = 1/4. Time = 4 days.

text: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 and 15 hours respectively. A leak can empty the tank in 20 hours. If all are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
A and B can complete a work in 8 and 12 days respectively. They work on alternate days, starting with A. In how many days will the work be completed?
explanation: A's rate = 1/8, B's rate = 1/12. In 2 days (one cycle): 1/8 + 1/12 = 5/24. After 4 cycles (8 days): 4×5/24 = 20/24 = 5/6. Remaining = 1/6. Day 9 (A works): 1/8. Since 1/8 < 1/6, remaining after day 9 = 1/6 − 1/8 = 1/24. Day 10 (B works): B needs 1/24 ÷ 1/12 = 1/2 day. Total = 9 + 1/2 = 9.5 days.

text: A, B, and C together can do a work in 6 days. A and B together take 10 days, B and C take 8 days. Find the time taken by A alone.
A and B together can do a work in 12 days. They work together for 3 days, then A leaves. B alone completes the remaining work in 18 days. Find the time taken by A alone.
explanation: A+B rate = 1/12. In 3 days: 3/12 = 1/4. Remaining = 3/4. B does 3/4 in 18 days. B's rate = 3/(4×18) = 3/72 = 1/24. A's rate = 1/12 − 1/24 = (2−1)/24 = 1/24. A alone = 24 days.

text: A can do a work in 10 days, B in 30 days. They start together, but A works only half the time B works. Find the total time to complete the work.
explanation: Let B work for t days. A works for t/2 days. Work done: (t/2)/10 + t/30 = 1. t/20 + t/30 = 1. LCM of 20,30 = 60. 3t/60 + 2t/60 = 5t/60 = t/12 = 1. t = 12 days.

text: A starts working alone and completes 1/4th of the work in 5 days. Then B joins, and together they finish the remaining work in 9 days. Find the time taken by B alone to do the whole work.
A contractor estimated that 12 workers can complete a work in 15 days. After 5 days, he realizes only 1/4th work is done. How many additional workers are required to complete the work on time?
explanation: 12 workers do 1/4 of work in 5 days. So at actual rate, full work = 12 × 5 × 4 = 240 worker-days. Remaining = 3/4 of work = 180 worker-days. Remaining time = 10 days. Workers needed = 180/10 = 18. Additional = 18 − 12 = 6.

text: A can do a work in 24 days, B in 16 days, C in 12 days. They work in this pattern: Day 1: A+B, Day 2: B+C, Day 3: A+C (repeats). In how many days will the work be completed?
A is three times as efficient as B. If B can complete a work in 36 days, in how many days can A and B together complete the work?
explanation: B's time = 36 days. A is 3 times as efficient, so A's time = 36/3 = 12 days. Together: 1/12 + 1/36 = (3+1)/36 = 4/36 = 1/9. Time = 9 days.

text: 4 men or 6 women can complete a work in 12 days. In how many days can 2 men and 3 women complete the same work?
explanation: 4 men in 12 days → 1 man's rate = 1/48 per day. 6 women in 12 days → 1 woman's rate = 1/72 per day. 4M = 6W → 1M = 1.5W. 2 men + 3 women = 2/48 + 3/72 = 1/24 + 1/24 = 2/24 = 1/12. Time = 12 days.

text: A can complete a piece of work in 15 days working 8 hours a day. B can complete the same work in 10 days working 8 hours a day. If they work together for 6 hours a day, how many days will they take?
explanation: A's total work = 15×8 = 120 man-hours. B's total work = 10×8 = 80 man-hours. A's rate = 1/120 per hour. B's rate = 1/80 per hour. Together per hour: 1/120 + 1/80 = (2+3)/240 = 5/240 = 1/48. Per day (6 hours): 6/48 = 1/8. Days = 8.

text: A does 40% of a work in 8 days. He then calls B, and they together finish the remaining work in 6 days. How long would B alone take to do the whole work?
explanation: A does 40% in 8 days. A's rate = 5% per day = 1/20 per day. Remaining = 60%. A+B do 60% in 6 days → 10% per day together. B's rate = 10% − 5% = 5% per day = 1/20. B alone = 20 days.

text: 12 men can complete a work in 18 days. After 6 days, 4 more men join. How many more days are needed to complete the remaining work?
explanation: Total work = 12×18 = 216 man-days. Work done in 6 days = 12×6 = 72 man-days. Remaining = 216−72 = 144 man-days. Now 16 men work: 144/16 = 9 days.

text: A and B can do a work in 12 days. B and C can do it in 15 days. C and A can do it in 20 days. In how many days can A, B, and C together do the work?
A pipe can fill a tank in 6 hours. Due to a leak at the bottom, the tank is filled in 8 hours. If the tank is full, how long will the leak take to empty the entire tank?
explanation: Pipe rate = 1/6. With leak: net rate = 1/8. Leak rate = 1/6 − 1/8 = (4−3)/24 = 1/24. Leak empties in 24 hours.

text: 20 workers can build a wall in 30 days. After 15 days, 5 workers leave. In how many more days will the remaining workers finish the wall?
explanation: Total work = 20×30 = 600 man-days. Done in 15 days = 20×15 = 300. Remaining = 300. Workers left = 15. Days = 300/15 = 20 days.

text: A works twice as fast as B. If B alone can complete a work in 36 days, in how many days can they complete it working together?
explanation: B = 36 days. A is twice as fast → A = 18 days. Together: 1/18 + 1/36 = (2+1)/36 = 3/36 = 1/12. Time = 12 days.

text: Pipe A fills a tank in 20 minutes, Pipe B fills it in 30 minutes. Pipe C empties it in 10 minutes. If A is opened at the start, B after 5 minutes, and C after 10 minutes, when will the tank be full?
explanation: A rate = 1/20, B rate = 1/30, C rate = −1/10. First 5 min (A only): 5/20 = 1/4. Next 5 min (A+B): 5×(1/20+1/30) = 5×5/60 = 25/60 = 5/12. After 10 min: 1/4+5/12 = 3/12+5/12 = 8/12 = 2/3. After 10 min (A+B+C): 1/20+1/30−1/10 = (3+2−6)/60 = −1/60 per min. Net rate is negative, so the tank drains. It will never fill.

text: A, B, and C can complete a work in 10, 15, and 20 days respectively. They take turns working one day each, starting with A, then B, then C. On which day will the work be completed?
If 6 men and 8 women can complete a work in 10 days, and 26 men and 48 women can complete the same work in 2 days, find the time taken by 15 men and 20 women to complete the work.
explanation: Let 1 man's daily work = m, 1 woman's daily work = w. (6m+8w)×10 = 1 → 60m+80w = 1. (26m+48w)×2 = 1 → 52m+96w = 1. From equations: 60m+80w = 52m+96w → 8m = 16w → m = 2w. Substituting: 60(2w)+80w = 1 → 200w = 1 → w = 1/200. m = 1/100. 15 men + 20 women = 15/100+20/200 = 15/100+10/100 = 25/100 = 1/4 per day. Time = 4 days.

text: A father can do a job as fast as his two sons working together. If one son does the job in 6 days and the other in 12 days, how many days does it take the father to do the job?
explanation: Son1 = 1/6, Son2 = 1/12. Together = 1/6+1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 per day. Father's rate = 1/4. Father alone = 4 days.

text: Two pipes can fill a tank in 15 hours and 20 hours respectively. A third pipe empties it in 30 hours. If all three are opened simultaneously and the tank was initially 1/5 full, how long to fill it completely?
A can do a work in 15 days and B in 20 days. They work together for 4 days, then A is replaced by C. The remaining work is done by B and C in 8 days. In how many days can C alone do the work?
A group of men decided to do a job in 10 days, but 5 of them became absent. The rest did the job in 12 days. Find the original number of men.
explanation: Let original = n men. Work = n×10 = (n−5)×12. 10n = 12n−60. 2n = 60. n = 30.

text: A tank has two inlet pipes A and B and one outlet pipe C. A can fill the tank in 12 hours, B in 15 hours, and C can empty it in 20 hours. If all three are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
X can do a piece of work in 40 days. He works at it for 8 days and then Y finishes the remaining work in 16 days. How long will X and Y together take to complete the work?
A machine can produce 100 items in 5 hours. After 3 hours of operation, it slows down and produces at 60% of its normal rate. How many total items are produced in 8 hours?
explanation: Normal rate = 100/5 = 20 items/hour. In first 3 hours: 3×20 = 60 items. Remaining 5 hours at 60% rate = 12 items/hour: 5×12 = 60 items. Total = 60+60 = 120 items.

text: To do a piece of work, B takes 3 times as long as A and C together and C twice as long as A and B together. If A, B and C together can complete the work in 10 days, how long would A take alone to complete it?
explanation: 3×(B's 1 day work) = (A+C)'s 1 day work. So 4×(B's work) = (A+B+C)'s work = 1/10. B = 1/40. Similarly, 3×(C's work) = (A+B+C)'s work = 1/10. C = 1/30. A = 1/10 − 1/40 − 1/30 = (12−3−4)/120 = 5/120 = 1/24. A alone = 24 days.

text: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days, B and C in 8 days and C and A in 6 days. How long would B alone take to do the same work?
A takes 5 days more than B and 9 days more than C to do a job. A and B together can do the job in the same time as C alone. How many days would A take to do it?
explanation: Let A take x days. B takes (x−5) days, C takes (x−9) days. A+B together = C: 1/x + 1/(x−5) = 1/(x−9). (2x−5)/[x(x−5)] = 1/(x−9). (2x−5)(x−9) = x(x−5). 2x²−23x+45 = x²−5x. x²−18x+45 = 0. (x−3)(x−15) = 0. Since x−9 > 0, x = 15 days.

text: A, B and C can separately do a work in 12, 15 and 20 days respectively. They started to work together but C left after 2 days. In how many more days will A and B finish the remaining work?

A, B and C together can complete a piece of work in 10 days. All three started working together and after 4 days A left. Then B and C together completed the work in 10 more days. A alone could complete the work in:
explanation: A+B+C = 1/10. Work done in 4 days = 4/10 = 2/5. Remaining = 3/5. B+C do 3/5 in 10 days, so B+C rate = 3/50. A's rate = 1/10 − 3/50 = (5−3)/50 = 2/50 = 1/25. A alone = 25 days.

text: A, B and C can complete a work separately in 24, 36 and 48 days respectively. They started together but C left after 4 days of start and A left 3 days before completion of the work. In how many days will the work be completed?
A and B can complete a piece of work in 12 and 18 days respectively. A begins to do the work and they work alternately one at a time for one day each. The whole work will be completed in:
explanation: A = 1/12, B = 1/18. In 2 days (one cycle): 1/12+1/18 = (3+2)/36 = 5/36. After 7 cycles (14 days): 7×5/36 = 35/36. Remaining = 1/36. Day 15 is A's turn. A does 1/12 per day. Time = (1/36)÷(1/12) = 1/3 day. Total = 14 + 1/3 = 14 1/3 days.

text: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 36, 54 and 72 days respectively. They started the work but A left 8 days before the completion of the work while B left 12 days before the completion. The number of days for which C worked is:
explanation: Let total days = x. A works (x−8) days, B works (x−12) days, C works x days. (x−8)/36 + (x−12)/54 + x/72 = 1. LCM = 216: 6(x−8)+4(x−12)+3x = 216. 6x−48+4x−48+3x = 216. 13x = 312. x = 24 days.

text: A contractor undertakes to do a piece of work in 40 days. He engages 100 men at the beginning and 100 more after 35 days and completes the work in stipulated time. If he had not engaged the additional men, how many days behind schedule would the work have been finished?
explanation: Total work = 100×35 + 200×5 = 3500+1000 = 4500 man-days. Without extra men: 4500/100 = 45 days. Behind schedule = 45−40 = 5 days.

text: A group of workers having equal efficiency can complete a job in 4 days. But every alternate day starting from the second day, 3 workers are withdrawn and every alternate day starting from the third day, 2 workers are added. If it now takes 7 days to complete the job, find the number of workers who started the job.
explanation: Let n workers start. Total work = 4n worker-days. Day 1: n, Day 2: n−3, Day 3: n−1, Day 4: n−4, Day 5: n−2, Day 6: n−5, Day 7: n−3. Sum = 7n−18. Set equal to 4n: 7n−18 = 4n. 3n = 18. n = 6.

text: 16 men can finish a piece of work in 49 days. 14 men started working and in 8 days they could finish a certain amount of work. If it is required to finish the remaining work in 24 days, how many more men should be added to the existing workforce?
explanation: Total work = 16×49 = 784 man-days. Work done by 14 men in 8 days = 14×8 = 112 man-days. Remaining = 784−112 = 672 man-days. Workers needed = 672/24 = 28. Additional = 28−14 = 14 men.
